test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 30 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: S gets 78, 75, 68, 64 and 58 marks in Hindi, English, Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics, respectively. What are his average marks per subject?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the assumed average be 70.

Net deviation from assumed average = (+8) + (+5) + (−2) + (−6) + (−12) = −7

Deviation per subject = −7 ÷ 5 = −1.4

Actual Average = 70 − 1.4 = 68.6 marks

**∴ The correct answer is 68.6 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks obtained by S in five subjects: Hindi = 78, English = 75, Chemistry = 68, Physics = 64, Mathematics = 58

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of marks = 78 + 75 + 68 + 64 + 58 = 343

⇒ Total subjects = 5

⇒ Average marks = 343 ÷ 5

⇒ Average marks = 68.6

**∴ The correct answer is 68.6 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Deviation Method for Averages

It simplifies large calculations by selecting an assumed mean and finding the net difference of all actual values from it. True Average = Assumed Mean + (Sum of Deviations ÷ Number of Values).

Weighted Average

Used when items have different counts or importance. Formula: Aw = (w₁×x₁ + w₂×x₂ + ... ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... ).

Combined Average

If group 1 has n₁ items with average A₁, and group 2 has n₂ items with average A₂, then the Combined Average = (n₁×A₁ + n₂×A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
